A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Noise2VST work, and all 11 pages of each are readable. Neither includes appendices or embedded supplementary files. v2 references supplementary proofs, ablations, and results that are absent, limiting comparison of those additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original Noise2VST denoising results on synthetic and real images, qualitative reconstructions, and runtime measurements in Figures 1–2 and Tables 1–5.

after.justification: v2 retains the original Noise2VST experiments, reconstructions, and runtime results. Results retained from v1 still constitute original empirical evidence.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same spline VST, affine-corrected inverse, blind-spot training, and ordinary-denoiser inference. Noise2VST† renames Noise2VST-light. The new statement that θ1 can be fixed to zero does not establish an implemented procedure change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Kodak, BSD300, Set14, fluorescence microscopy data, W2S, and SIDD under the same stated task coverage. FMDD becomes FMD without changing the represented dataset or selected microscopy subsets.

E2.justification: v2 adds FBI-D to the three microscopy comparisons in Table 2 and the SIDD benchmark comparison in Table 4; no SIDD validation score is supplied for it. Existing comparison methods are retained.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 changes the stated synthetic Poisson parameterization from (a,b)=(λ,0) to (1/λ,0), retaining λ in [5,50]. This corrects a reported setting but does not establish that experiments were rerun. Splits, preprocessing, metrics, and training budgets otherwise remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 newly references an inverse-transform ablation and supplementary explanations or analyses of variance stabilization and denoiser behavior. The referenced material is absent, preventing verification of the analyses and their extent. The displayed qualitative cases remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both retain 10, 3, and 20 repetitions of the synthetic datasets with different noise instances. No seed information, uncertainty intervals, error bars, or statistical tests are added to the supplied results.

E6.justification: New FBI-D PSNR/SSIM entries are 32.22/0.885, 38.32/0.964, and 33.95/0.908 in Table 2, and 50.57/0.990 for SIDD benchmark in Table 4. Existing numerical entries are unchanged. Section 4.2 revises the stated maximum baseline gap from 0.05 to 0.06 dB without changing Table 1.

T1.justification: v2 newly asserts that θ1 can be fixed to zero without loss of generality and references supplementary proofs concerning this and the fixed denoiser noise level. The displayed equations remain unchanged, but the missing supplementary material prevents assessment of the proof additions and their substance.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: learning a model-free VST from one noisy image, reusing frozen Gaussian denoisers, and achieving competitive or superior denoising at limited computational cost.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 adds under- and over-exposure as perturbations beyond the standard photon/read-noise description and uses them to explain the flexibility of a model-free VST. This extends the interpretation without reporting a new exposure-specific experiment.

D1.justification: v2 adds a source-code repository address in Section 4.1 and acknowledges IDRIS/GENCI computing resources. Existing implementation, hyperparameter, hardware, and runtime disclosures are retained; the repository itself was not accessed.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to FBI-denoiser and VST-Net and explicitly acknowledges earlier combinations of deep learning and VSTs in Section 3.1. The previous references and overall research positioning are retained.

P1.justification: v2 renames the fast variant, standardizes FMD terminology, updates affiliation and acknowledgment text, and adds short explanations and supplementary cross-references. Section order and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Tables 2 and 4 gain FBI-D rows, and Tables 1–4 reorder the Noise2VST variants. Figure 2 gains a supplementary-material pointer in its caption. Margins, hyperlink colors, and text flow change modestly; the same two figures and five tables are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reporting through the Poisson parameter correction, added FBI-D comparisons, acknowledgment of related VST methods, and code-access information. These are useful but limited gains because the method and existing experimental evidence remain stable. The absent supplementary material prevents crediting the referenced proofs and ablations as verified improvements.
